description: Structural, mātrā, Kannada aṃśa, and Telugu deśi-gaṇa meter rules that cannot be represented as one fixed Guru/Laghu string.
prominenceNote: Editorial prominence is only a tie-breaker between candidates with comparable observed metrical evidence; it never overrides an exact or stronger fit.

fixedMeterSource.title: Kannada fixed-vṛtta derivations
fixedMeterSource.notes: The cited formulas describe Campakamāle and Mahāsragdharā as the Kannada counterparts formed by replacing the initial Guru of Utpalamālikā and Sragdharā with two Laghus.

meters.name: anuṣṭubh (pathyā)
meters.notes: This rule set recognizes pathyā Anuṣṭubh in four one-pāda lines or two complete 8+8 half-verse units. Vipulā variations are not yet accepted.

source.title: A Study on the Sanskrit Meter: Anuṣṭubh

meters.name: kanda (Kannada)
signatureLines: gaṇas 6 & 14: LGL or LLLL; 8 & 16 end G
meters.notes: Implements the rhythmic, yati, and dvitīyākṣara-prāsa rules in the cited rule packet. On lines 2 and 4 only, a final written Laghu may satisfy the required terminal Guru through pādānta lengthening. The entry remains provisional until the golden corpus is approved.

meters.name: pañcamātrā chaupadi (Kagga form)
signatureLines: the final written Laghu may lengthen at the line ending
meters.notes: Recognizes the modal written-text frame used by D. V. Gundappa's Mankuthimmana Kagga, including opening dvitīyākṣara-prāsa and line-ending antya-prāsa. It is intentionally narrower than the broader historical mātrā-chaupadi family. Recitational lengthening, śithila-dvitva, and less common variants await an expert-reviewed corpus.

meters.name: śara ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks all six quantitative lines and their short/extended relationship. On extended lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening; a resolved Laghu pair remains valid. Literary constraints remain provisional.

meters.name: kusuma ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks all six quantitative lines and their short/extended relationship. On extended lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening; a resolved Laghu pair remains valid. Literary constraints remain provisional.

meters.name: bhoga ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks all six quantitative lines and their short/extended relationship. On extended lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening; a resolved Laghu pair remains valid. Literary constraints remain provisional.

meters.name: bhāminī ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks the alternating three/four-mātrā gaṇas across the complete six-line verse. On extended lines 3 and 6, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening. Literary constraints remain provisional pending expert corpus review.

meters.name: parivardhinī ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks all six quantitative lines, including the extended third and sixth lines. On lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening. Literary constraints remain provisional pending expert corpus review.

meters.name: vārdhaka ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks four five-mātrā gaṇas in the short lines and six plus the final cadence in lines three and six. On lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may fill the terminal Guru by pādānta lengthening. Literary constraints remain provisional.

meters.name: tripadi (Kannada)
signatureLines: VVVV | VBVV | VBV; gaṇas 6 and 10 are Brahma
meters.notes: Checks the core aṃśa frame, required Brahma positions, opening dvitīyākṣara-prāsa, and its internal recurrence in the first line's third gaṇa. Sung and folk substitutions remain explicitly provisional.

meters.name: folk tripadi (Kannada)
signatureLines: 5555 | 5455 | 545; gaṇa-final Laghu may be sung long (ಽ)
uncheckedRules: expansion and elision beyond one mātrā
meters.notes: Recognizes the later folk mātrā frame independently of classical aṃśa Tripadi. A gaṇa-final Laghu may supply one inferred sung mātrā; the analyzer marks that realization with a superscript avagraha without changing the poem.

meters.name: sāṅgatya
meters.notes: Checks the common Sāṅgatya aṃśa frame and opening dvitīyākṣara-prāsa. Melodic substitutions are historically normal and remain compatible rather than being silently rejected as a complete rule.

meters.name: piriyakkara
meters.notes: Checks the classical seven-gaṇa frame and the specifically documented Brahma alternatives in positions two and four. Broader sung substitutions remain unchecked.

meters.name: doreyakkara
meters.notes: Checks the classical six-gaṇa frame. The source records broad optional substitutions, which await an expert-reviewed corpus.

meters.name: naḍuvaṇakkara
meters.notes: Checks the classical five-gaṇa frame. Optional sung substitutions remain explicitly provisional.

meters.name: eḍeyakkara
meters.notes: Checks the classical four-gaṇa frame. Optional sung substitutions remain explicitly provisional.

meters.name: kiriyakkara
meters.notes: Checks the classical three-gaṇa frame. Optional sung substitutions remain explicitly provisional.

meters.name: eḷe (Kannada)
meters.notes: Checks the two-line aṃśa frame, first-line yati, opening dvitīyākṣara-prāsa, and the internal recurrence in the first line's third gaṇa.

meters.name: mātrā tripadi (historical Kannada)
meters.notes: Represents the historical mātrā-gaṇa Tripadi frame separately from both classical aṃśa Tripadi and the later folk 5555 | 5455 | 545 realization.

meters.name: aṃśa chaupadi (Kannada)
meters.notes: Checks the compact V+R aṃśa frame described for Kannada Chaupadi. It remains distinct from Kagga's narrower pañcamātrā form.

meters.name: mātrā chaupadi (historical Kannada)
meters.notes: Checks the broader historical 5+5+5+3 mātrā Chaupadi family without conflating it with the modal Kagga stanza.

meters.name: aṃśa ṣaṭpadi
signatureLines: VV | VV | VVR / VV | VV | VVR
meters.notes: Checks the complete six-line aṃśa Ṣaṭpadi frame and supplies karṣaṇa guidance for each matched aṃśa.

meters.name: uddaṇḍa ṣaṭpadi
meters.notes: Checks the five/five/eight four-mātrā-gaṇa arrangement over all six lines. On lines 3 and 6 only, a final written Laghu may provide the thirty-second mātrā by pādānta lengthening. Literary and recitational variants remain provisional.

meters.name: sobagina sone
meters.notes: Checks the VVVV/VVV paired pattern and keeps this song form distinct from Sāṅgatya's VVVV/VVB cadence.

meters.name: chandovatamsa (Nāgavarma)
meters.notes: Keeps Nāgavarma's three Viṣṇu plus one Brahma signature canonical while accepting the reviewed VRVB second line and VVVV third line as unmarked contracted realizations. Jayakīrti's different VBBBB frame is cataloged separately as Ādivarāha.

meters.name: ādivarāha (Jayakīrti)
meters.notes: Uses the Jayakīrti VBBBB signature under the distinct Ādivarāha name, avoiding a collision with Nāgavarma's Chandovatamsa.

meters.name: akkarike (Nāgavarma)
meters.notes: Implements Nāgavarma's V-B-V-B-V-R aṃśa signature. Historical yati placement remains advisory until a larger approved corpus is available.

meters.name: madanavatī (Nāgavarma)
meters.notes: Implements Nāgavarma's primary five-Viṣṇu-plus-Guru realization. A final written Laghu may fill the literal terminal Guru on each of the four pādas by pādānta lengthening. The equal-mātrā 4V+R division is documented but remains unchecked until whole-line alternative aṃśa divisions are supported.

meters.name: mandānila ragaḷe
signatureLines: a gaṇa may not begin LG; adjacent lines use antya-prāsa
meters.notes: Checks repeatable line rhythm, the documented 3+5 alternative, lagam restriction, and pairwise end-rhyme. The entry remains provisional pending expert review.

meters.name: utsāha ragaḷe
signatureLines: unbounded lines; 4 or 8 gaṇas per line
meters.notes: Checks either four or eight three-mātrā gaṇas on every written line and pairwise end-rhyme. The entry remains provisional pending expert review.

meters.name: lalita ragaḷe
meters.notes: Checks four five-mātrā gaṇas on every written line and pairwise end-rhyme. The entry remains provisional pending expert review.

meters.name: āṭaveladi (Telugu)
signatureLines: S = Sūrya; I = Indra; yati joins gaṇas 1 and 4
meters.notes: The canonical Vemana/śataka frame. Prāsa is not required; full traditional yati-maitri equivalence is reported conservatively.

meters.name: tēṭagīti (Telugu)
signatureLines: 4 pādas × S I I S S
meters.notes: One Sūrya, two Indra, and two Sūrya gaṇas in every pāda. Prāsa is not required.

meters.name: kandamu (Telugu)
signatureLines: gaṇas 6 & 14: LGL or LLLL; 8 & 16 end G
meters.notes: A distinct Telugu rule entry: it shares the 3/5/3/5 four-mātrā skeleton with Kannada Kanda but retains Telugu terminology, yati, and prāsa provenance.

meters.name: dvipada (Telugu)
signatureLines: yati joins the openings of gaṇas 1 and 3; dvitīyākṣara-prāsa joins the pair
meters.notes: The regular Telugu narrative couplet. Manjari dvipada is the same rhythmic frame without compulsory dvitīyākṣara-prāsa.

meters.name: mañjarī dvipada (Telugu)
meters.notes: The prāsa-free relative of dvipada; historical practice may use prāsa-yati.

meters.name: sīsamu (Telugu)
signatureLines: 4 long pādas × I I I I I I S S
each long pāda may be written as 4+4 gaṇa half-lines
normally followed by a 4-pāda āṭaveladi or tēṭagīti ettugīti
meters.notes: Recognizes the four-long-line and eight-half-line conventions, plus canonical āṭaveladi or tēṭagīti ettugīti layouts. Prāsa is optional.

meters.name: mutyāla sarālu (Telugu)
meters.notes: Gurajada's four-line song gait. The closing line may contain any total from seven through fourteen mātrās; word music remains an essential part of the form.

meters.name: taruvoja (Telugu)
signatureLines: 4 long pādas × (I I I S) + (I I I S)
may be displayed as 8 dvipada-like half-lines
meters.notes: The traditional extended-dvipada frame. Historical descriptions differ in how the written long lines and prāsa-governed half-lines are counted.

meters.name: madhyākkara (Telugu)
signatureLines: 4 long pādas × (I I S) + (I I S)
yati at the fourth gaṇa; prāsa required
meters.notes: Nannaya's naturalized akkara form as described by Brown; later handbooks sometimes place the internal yati on the fifth rather than fourth gaṇa.

meters.name: hayapracāra ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 3+3+3+3 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: turagavalgana ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: eight 3-mātrā gaṇas; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: vijayamaṅgala ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: sixteen 3-mātrā gaṇas; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: madhuragati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 4+4+4+4 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: harigati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: eight 4-mātrā gaṇas; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: dviradagati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 5+5+5+5 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: vijayabhadra ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: eight 5-mātrā gaṇas; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: hariṇagati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 3+4+3+4 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: vṛṣabhagati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 3+4+3+4+3+4+3+4 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme

meters.name: haṃsagati ragaḍa (Telugu)
signatureLines: each line: 5+5+3+3 mātrās; couplet prāsa and end-rhyme
